Her honor student image from school crumbles inside of me.

二人と肩を並べて歩くのは非常に抵抗があったので、早足で横道に入った。

Deeply uncomfortable walking shoulder to shoulder with the two of them, I quicken my pace and turn down a side street.

They follow without a word of complaint.

pages.en:
Perhaps it is the setting of a park at night.

In profile, looking up at the bridge, Tohsaka seems more beautiful than she ever does at school.

It's hard to know what to do with myself.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Maybe it’s just because it’s nighttime.
Tohsaka’s face, looking up at the bridge, seems even more beautiful than at school… I’m troubled.

pages.ja:

公園で立ち止まっている遠坂を促して階段を上る。
橋の横の歩道にさえ辿り着けば、あとは新都まで一直線だ。

pages.en:
“Come on. We didn't come here to sightsee.”

I urge Tohsaka away from the park and climb the stairs.

Once we reach the pedestrian path along the bridge, it is a straight walk to Shinto.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Let’s go. We didn’t come here to play around.”
I hurry Tohsaka, who is standing still in the park, and make my way up the stairs.
Once we reach the road alongside the bridge, Shinto will be straight ahead of us.

歩道橋に人影はない。
それも当然、昼間でさえここを使う人は少ないのだ。
隣町まではバスか電車で行くのが普通で、この歩道橋はあまり使われない。

pages.en:
There is no one on the footbridge.

Naturally enough. Few people use it even during the day.

Most travel to the next town by bus or train, and the footbridge sees little traffic.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There’s no one on the bridge.

なにしろ距離があまりにも長いし、どうも作りが頑丈でないというか、いつ崩れてもおかしくないのでは、なんて不安を呼び起こす。
ロケーション的には文句無しなのにデートコースに使われないのも、そのあたりが原因だろう。

pages.en:
The distance is simply too great. Worse, the bridge does not feel especially sturdy. It inspires the uneasy suspicion that it might collapse at any moment.

The view itself is beyond reproach. That it never became a popular destination for dates is probably the fault of its construction.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s because it’s so long, and it carries a fear that it might collapse on you.
That must be why this place isn’t used for dates, even though it’s perfect location-wise.

「……馬鹿らしい。なに考えてんだ、俺」
無言で後を付いてくるセイバーと、すぐ横で肩を並べている遠坂。

Saber follows silently, and Tohsaka walks abreast of me.

I try not to be conscious of either girl and increase my pace, intent only on crossing the bridge as quickly as possible.
pages.mirrorMoon:

When I think of Shinto, I picture only the office district around the station, where development never seems to end. Leave the station behind, however, and traces of the old town remain.

Beyond the bridge, Tohsaka leads us into the suburbs.

The farther we ascend, the fewer buildings we pass, until a foreign cemetery built into the hillside comes into view.

The suburbs are the oldest of all.

As you go farther up the hill, there are fewer buildings and the foreigners’ cemetery built on the slope can be seen.

Tohsaka walks on ahead up the hill.

The church on the hill.

I never imagined that my first visit to a house of God I had always ignored would be for a purpose like this.

pages.jaRuby:

広い、荘厳な礼拝堂だった。
これだけの席があるという事は、日中に訪れる人々の数も多いという事だろう。
これほどの教会を任されているのだから、ここの神父はよほどの人格者と見える。

The chapel is vast and solemn.

Any priest entrusted with a church like this must surely be a man of exceptional character.

For convenience, let us call the hidden face of the world’s great religion—the church that an ordinary person could live and die without ever seeing—the Holy Church.

The two appear similar but are nothing alike. Officially they cooperate; in practice, each will gladly murder the other whenever an opening presents itself.

and the other side of religion, the side you wouldn’t see while living a normal life, is called the Holy Church.

It hunts down those who are human in shape but not in nature, and practitioners of magecraft are counted among its targets.

Within the Church, miracles are the province of a chosen few among the saints.

Any miracle wielded by another is heresy.

They totally eliminate the inhuman, and they count magic-using humans among their targets.
For the church, miracles are only given to holy saints. Any miracles performed by other people are heresies.
